title: ia capture writes the admitted snapshot; ia compile is deprecated in its favour
summary: The new ia capture [--json] command admits the workspace and writes its snapshot to .ia/work/snapshot/current.json in the ia-snapshot-1 format: one JSON document with sorted keys holding format, language, kernelDigest, revision, the admitted records sorted by identity with their per-record digest, one {identity, root, band, digest} capture membership row per record, the diagnostics ordered by path, line, code and message, and their counts. The pair is written by @inventarch/db (writeCapture), and every db handle seeds its previous snapshot from it. .ia/work/snapshot/previous.json holds the most recent capture whose revision differs from the current one: a capture at a new revision renames the prior current.json there byte for byte, even when no record's digest changed, and a capture at an unchanged revision keeps previous.json as it is while it holds a capture at another revision. With no readable prior capture (the first one, or a current.json that is not an ia-snapshot-1 capture, which the capture names and replaces), a previous.json at another revision is kept as the most recent capture there is; a previous.json at the new revision, or one that is no capture, is removed once current.json is written. The new bytes are staged in a temporary file before either file is replaced, a failed write leaves both files as they were, a current.json that already holds the capture's bytes is not rewritten, and only .ia/work/snapshot/ is written; .ia/src is never touched. ia capture adds no ignore rule; fresh ia init creates .ia/.gitignore with work/ and distributions/ only when that file is absent, and preserves an existing ignore file. The report gives the revision, the record count and how each record's digest compares with the prior capture's current.json, as changed, unchanged, new and removed, so two captures with no edit between them report 0 changed and a first capture reports every record new. With --json the report is {version, snapshot, format, revision, digest, records, changed, unchanged, new, removed, prior, ignored, previous, rotated, admission}: it adds the snapshot's path and SHA-256, the prior revision it compared with, why an existing current.json was not taken as a capture, the retained previous capture, whether this capture rotated it, and admission as {status, errors, warnings, notEvaluated}. Findings in a source the workspace authors never stop the write: a workspace with errors is still captured, the effect line carries a warning symbol and the command exits 1. Two cases refuse before anything is written, keeping both files: a floor or seed input (the floor, an installed package or an adopted mount) that fails to parse, which is a syntax error the language's scanner or parser reports, refuses with that finding's code, located at it, exit 3, naming ia validate, while any other finding there, such as a keyword two adopted systems both register, is written into the snapshot like a finding in the workspace's own sources; a directory whose own .ia/src declares no `@workspace` refuses as IA-DB-ROOT-INVALID (exit 3). It names ia validate when its own sources have errors; otherwise an initialized root with .ia/release.json is told to restore its authored `@workspace` source under .ia/src from source control and run ia position --root <root>, while a root without a release descriptor names ia init for that directory. A composition.sources entry that names no root, or a path selection that selects nothing, is written as an IA-COMP-FIELD-VALUE warning at its line, as ia validate reports it. A link or junction on the snapshot path, an entry at .ia/work or .ia/work/snapshot that is not a directory, or an entry at either snapshot path that is not a regular file, refuses with IA-DB-PATH-UNSAFE (exit 3), located at an entry that is not a directory or not a regular file (@inventarch/db DbError gains an optional path naming it; a link is named in the message), and names ia capture for that root. A write the system refuses for a permission, a busy or read-only entry, or an entry of the wrong kind is IA-CLI-FAILED (exit 3), located at and naming what to make writable before ia capture: the read-only or open snapshot file a rename failed on, on Windows, and otherwise the directory the write creates, renames or removes entries in; another system error, such as a full disk, takes the generic next. A failed write leaves the pair it found, also when the capture would drop a previous.json that is no capture or one at the new revision: that file is moved aside first and restored. Concurrent captures of one root are last-writer-wins. ia compile is deprecated in favour of ia capture and unchanged in 1.x: it still writes the ia.compiled.v1 artifact to .ia/work/compiled.json or --out <file> under .ia/work/, prints it alone with --stdout, refuses an existing artifact with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION unless --force, prints {version, artifact, revision, digest, counts} with --json and keeps its exit codes. Whenever it runs to a result it now prints one deprecation line on stderr naming ia capture, in every output mode, --json and --stdout included, so stdout is what 1.x wrote; a refusal prints only the refusal. It never writes the capture's snapshot, and ia capture never writes the artifact. In 2.0 ia compile becomes a deprecated alias of ia capture, removed in 3.0. @inventarch/cli/internal/compile exports runCompile and the ia.compiled.v1 builders unchanged, and adds DEPRECATION, the line it prints.
